sources.entry: Stoat - Stoat is a user-first chat platform built with modern web technologies. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0/MIT Rust
Stoat (formerly Revolt) | Chat platform for communities, a Discord alternative

summary.one_liner: Docker Compose configuration and guide for self-hosting a full Stoat (formerly Revolt) chat instance, including back-end, web front-end, file server, and metadata/image proxy.
summary.what_it_does: This repository provides configuration files and step-by-step instructions for deploying a complete Stoat chat instance using Docker. The deployment covers the back-end, web front-end, file server, and metadata and image proxy. A generate_config.sh script creates secrets in secrets.env and a Revolt.toml configuration file, which can be edited by hand. The stack is started with docker compose, and updates are applied by pulling the repo, regenerating config, and pulling new images. The README also includes optional tweaks such as placing Stoat behind another reverse proxy, pinning MongoDB 4.4 or using valkey instead of KeyDB, and exposing the database port. It also lists migration notices and security advisory versions for the backend and web client.
use_cases: host my own Discord-style chat server
run a private community chat on my own VPS
self-host a chat platform with voice and video
set up a Revolt-compatible chat instance
how_to_run: Point your domain's A/AAAA records (or CNAME) at the server
Install git and Docker (docker-ce with docker-compose-plugin) on Ubuntu Server
git clone the stoat repository and cd into it
docker compose up (or docker compose up -d to run detached)
notable: Single script (generate_config.sh) generates secrets and configuration for the whole stack
Bundles back-end, web front-end, file server and metadata/image proxy in one deployment
Documented compatibility swaps for older CPUs (MongoDB 4.4) and ARM systems (valkey)
Caddy reverse proxy with an option to sit behind another reverse proxy on port 8880
Detailed upgrade notices for breaking changes dated 2022 through 2026
caveats: Most official clients do not support self-hosted instances; the web client and PWA are the best-supported options
Video streaming above the configured Revolt.toml size limit kicks users (documented incomplete implementation)
Ports 7881/tcp and 50000-50100/udp must be open to the internet for LiveKit voice/video; Docker bypasses ufw rules
Losing secrets.env can make all files on the instance inaccessible; upgrades from before Feb 2026 require manual secret migration
keywords: host a chat for my community
